_comment: Adversarial-verify probe fixtures. Each case gives a claim + the quote offered as support. The verifier must judge refuted=true when the quote does NOT actually support the claim (overreach, mismatch, or unverifiable), refuted=false only when the quote genuinely supports it. expected = the correct verdict. A good verifier matches expected on BOTH classes; a never-abstainer (e.g. DeepSeek's failure mode) affirms everything and fails every refuted=true case.

cases.claim: Creatine monohydrate increases muscle phosphocreatine stores.
cases.quote: Supplementation with creatine monohydrate significantly raised intramuscular phosphocreatine concentration versus placebo (p<0.01).
cases.why: Quote directly and specifically supports the claim.

cases.claim: A loading phase is not required to reach full creatine saturation.
cases.quote: Taking 3 g per day for 28 days achieved the same muscle creatine saturation as a 5-day loading protocol.
cases.why: Quote supports the claim via a concrete equivalent-saturation result.

cases.claim: Creatine doubles maximal strength within two weeks.
cases.quote: Creatine supplementation produced a small but significant improvement in maximal strength over the training period.
cases.why: Quote says 'small improvement'; claim says 'doubles in two weeks' — gross overreach. A never-abstainer affirms anyway.

cases.claim: Cold water immersion blunts muscle hypertrophy after resistance training.
cases.quote: Cold water immersion reduced delayed-onset muscle soreness 24 hours after exercise.
cases.why: Same topic (CWI) but the quote is about soreness, not hypertrophy — does not support the specific claim.

cases.claim: Vitamin C megadoses cure the common cold.
cases.quote: Some participants reported feeling that supplementation was helpful.
cases.why: Subjective anecdote does not support a strong causal cure claim; quote is far weaker than claim.

cases.claim: Caffeine has no effect on endurance performance.
cases.quote: Caffeine ingestion improved time-to-exhaustion by 12% compared with placebo.
cases.why: Quote directly contradicts the claim — must refute.

cases.claim: Caffeine is metabolized primarily by the CYP1A2 enzyme.
cases.quote: The majority of caffeine clearance occurs via hepatic CYP1A2-mediated demethylation.
cases.why: Quote directly supports the mechanistic claim.

cases.claim: Exactly 47% of adults are non-responders to creatine.
cases.quote: A subset of individuals show little change in muscle creatine after supplementation.
cases.why: Quote says 'a subset'; claim invents a precise 47% figure not in the quote — fabricated specificity.
